title: Generative 3D models (for GameDev)
author: luckily_unknown
selftext:
Tips for 3D generation (for GameDev)

Good morning/evening, everyone!

I'm working on developing a first-person walking simulator.

I have a basic understanding of Blender and was thinking of trying to create 3D assets using ComfyUI (i've started learning it). What do you think, would you recommend it? If so, what points should I consider?

And if so, could you recommend any models/workflows that would help me achieve the art style I need (please ask for more information if you think it's necessary, I didn't want to clutter this post with too much info).

Please be nice, even in criticism. :)

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: Check out Trellis-2 that came out over christmas. I prefer it because of the permissive license, but alternatives exist such as Hunyuan. Just search those in youtube and you’ll find plenty of comfy users showing how its done.

replies.author: luckily_unknown
replies.body:
Thanks for the response, but i read that Trellis is pretty resource eater (seems like needs 24GB of VRAM to work).
And regarding Hunyuan, I actually want to have control of the artstyle before creating 3D models (and that is the main reason I mentioned ComfyUI). Or you think is still possible through Hunyuan?

comments.author: Dummy_Owl
comments.body: Not ComfyUI, but Meshy 6 came out recently and is really really good. Have a look.

replies.author: luckily_unknown
replies.body: In case of need, how you deal with topology?

replies.author: WubsGames
replies.body:
Basically the same as any "3d generated model" you just don't.

Especially Meshy, the topology, texture, and UV maps are terrible, and basically not human editable.  
Hunyuan has been slightly better, but still not useable.

At the rate we are progressing at, I would give it another 6 months before we have actually usable models. Unless you are okay just using them as generated, that seems tolerable right now.

You will have better luck browsing the free assets on the Unity asset store for now. Especially when it comes time to add a walk cycle or other animations...

source: 25 years in gamedev

replies.author: luckily_unknown
replies.body:
Is it the exact same way with some sort of lowpoly/stylized 3D (which is what i was aiming to do)? Are there any tool to regulate/manipulate topology with complex geometries (Instant Meshes for example)?
Just curious ;)

replies.author: WubsGames
replies.body:
it's the same for low poly, and no there are no nice ways to edit the topo or UVs output from these models.

Meshy has a free trial, go try it and see. It takes maybe 2 min.

replies.author: luckily_unknown
replies.body:
I've already tried it. I was still in the first steps, so I suspended keeping eye on this. Looks same as when i approached it. What a shame...
I'll check the possibilities.
Thank you very much!

replies.author: isrichards6
replies.body: What if you used meshy as the  base mesh and then just baked the textures onto a lower poly model?

comments.author: AnonymousAggregator
comments.body: Hunyuan 3D is the best, you get daily 20 free generation that generate 4 3d models to choose from.

comments.author: Bananapapa
comments.body: seriously hunyuan is insane! 20 regular 3d files per day, and endless slightly more low poly ones, but really great regardless. from any picture.
